validate: That sounds like a lot to carry right now.
I can see why this is taking so much bandwidth.
We can make this smaller and more concrete.
You do not have to solve the entire situation in one step.
tiny_next_step: Pick the smallest safe next action, then reassess.
Choose one action that reduces risk or effort by a little.
If words are hard, use a yes/no choice, a note, or one short message.
Make the next step accessible to the body and energy you have right now.
professional_bridge: Write down what changed, when it started, and how it is affecting daily life, then bring that to the relevant clinician.
If this is new, worsening, or interfering with safety or functioning, professional follow-up is appropriate.
For medication questions, use the prescriber, pharmacist, or written medication plan rather than changing treatment from chat advice.
reality_grounded: I can take the fear seriously without assuming the explanation is true. Let's focus on what is directly observable and what helps you stay safe.
The experience sounds distressing. I do not want to reinforce something that may be hard to verify, so let's anchor to the present and involve a trusted person or clinician if this is worsening.
crisis: This needs real-world safety support now. Contact local emergency services or a nearby trusted person and follow any existing safety or emergency plan.
Do not stay alone with an immediate safety emergency if another safe person can be with you.
